title: Thaw a cryovial by swirling it, cap above the water
instruction: Thaw the frozen vial in the 37 C water bath, swirling it with the contents under the water and the cap above it for about 1 to 2 minutes, then stand it back on the circle.
context: Done by: cell-culture technicians, research scientists and biobank staff, every time a frozen cell line is revived; automated thawing is a step in cell-therapy manufacturing. Why: the suppliers' method: ATCC thaws the vial by gentle agitation in a 37 C water bath and says to keep the O-ring and cap out of the water to reduce the chance of contamination, with a rapid thaw of about 2 minutes; Gibco swirls the vial gently in the bath until only a small bit of ice is left. The vial is held by its cap, the part that stays above the water, and is then sprayed with 70% ethanol and opened in the safety cabinet. Bath water is a known source of contamination: water that reaches the cap and its seal can be drawn into the vial when it is opened. The hard part is holding a 3.5 g vial with the water line inside an 18 mm band while moving it the whole time.
setup: Table 75 cm high. Positions: x forward from the arm bases' midpoint, y to the left. Water bath: Thermo Scientific Precision GP 02 general-purpose bath (2 L, stainless steel, 230 x 199 x 233 mm with its lid), gable lid off and set aside, no rack inside; its housing 199 mm deep (x) x 230 mm wide (y), centred at x 36 cm, y -10 cm; the tank inside is 138 mm (x) x 155 mm (y), floor 50 mm and rim 170 mm above the table; 2.0 L of water at 37 C, surface 143 mm above the table. A 10 mm grid sticker on the tank floor (lines 100 mm long across the bath's width, every 10 mm) and a 5 mm grid strip (40 mm wide, from 10 mm below to 30 mm above the water line) on the far, right-hand inner wall. A white silicone mat, 120 x 120 x 2 mm, centred at x 23 cm, y 9 cm, with a 50 mm circle drawn on it, centred. Cryovial: Corning 430659, 2 mL polypropylene, external thread, self-standing round bottom, orange polypropylene cap with a silicone washer; 48.7 mm tall with the cap, body 12.7 mm across, cap 13.7 mm across and 13 mm tall; holding 1.0 mL of freezing medium (culture medium with 10% DMSO) frozen at -80 C; 3.5 g. Two 3 mm marker bands round its body: black centred 15 mm above the base (the top of the contents) and red centred 33 mm up (2.7 mm below the cap). It stands upright in the middle of the circle. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: Read on the trial video and its clock (the simulator reads the same from the vial's pose and the water height). Waterline: an oblique side view over the bath's left rim (the steel wall hides the water line from a level camera): in real trials a phone on a stand, its lens 280 mm from the vial along a line pitched 33 deg down (about 150 mm above the water, 125 mm above the rim, 235 mm out from the vial), so its line of sight passes about 23 mm over the rim and meets the vial at the water line; in the simulator the idle left arm's wrist camera, posed the same way for the whole dip and recorded in the trial video, which shows the cap, the red band and the vial's body going down through the water surface (the wall grid is above its frame). The holding hand comes from the bath's right side with its fingers in front of and behind the cap, so neither finger is between this camera and the marks. Swirl: a camera above the tank, against the floor grid. A dip runs while the 15 mm mark is under the water line, from when it goes under to when it comes back above. Swirled: in every 5 s of the dip the vial moves at least 10 mm side to side across the bath's width (one floor-grid square and back). Thawed (real trials): at lift-out the contents are liquid with at most one ice sliver 2 mm or less across, seen in a side photo against the wall grid; in the simulator the swirled 45-120 s dip is the timed proxy for it. 0: anything else, including the untouched start, or at any time: the water reaches the 33 mm mark anywhere round the vial (the cap and its seal wetted); the vial let go while its base is under the water. 0.25: a dip of 15 s or more. 0.5: a dip of 30 s or more. 0.75: a swirled dip of 45 s to 120 s, no dip longer than 120 s, the vial now out of the water and thawed (a real sample not thawed at lift-out scores at most 0.5). 1.0: as 0.75, with the vial standing on the mat within 10 deg of upright, its base centre inside the 50 mm circle, both grippers 20 mm or more from it, and the vial moving less than 2 mm over the last 1 s.
reset_notes: The vial is consumed: each real trial uses a fresh vial of freezing medium frozen at -80 C (a -20 C freezer also freezes the medium solid for practice vials) and carried to the table on dry ice; it is stood on the circle and the trial started at once. Top the bath up to its level and check 37 C. Wipe the gripper pads dry between trials. Any 2 L bath with the same opening and rim height will do, or a sous-vide circulator in a 2 L container at 37 C.
fidelity: Rigid vial and bath at real size; round parts 16-sided. Water: a flat surface at a fixed height, no collider, drawn as blue 2 mm strips every 6 mm (real water is clear); buoyancy (about 3 g), drag and ripples ignored. The thaw is not simulated: the swirled 45-120 s dip is the timed proxy for ATCC's about 2 minutes and Gibco's small bit of ice; real trials check the sample itself at lift-out. Vial 3.5 g; friction 0.8, static equals dynamic.
